relevance_reason: Reports new families with the TTN p.C30071R founder mutation and novel FN3 domain variants causing HMERF/MFM, with clinical, MRI, pathology and haplotype data.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) screened 127 unrelated UK probands with undiagnosed myopathy compatible with myofibrillar myopathy (MFM) by Sanger sequencing of the 119th FN3 domain and part of the kinase domain of TTN. The heterozygous g.274375T>C (p.C30071R) mutation was found in 5 of 127 (3.9%) probands, including 4 of 72 with a clinical diagnosis of MFM (5.5%); it cosegregated with disease in families F.1, F.2, and F.4. No patients had mutations at p.32450 in the kinase domain.
quotes: Sequencing identified the heterozygous g.274375T>C mutation (p.C30071R) in 5/127 unrelated subjects (F.1A, F.2A, F3, F.4B and F.5) with a total detection rate of 3.9% in the entire cohort.
The TTN gene changes co-segregated with the disease in families F.1, F.2, and F.4 (Figure 1).
Sequencing for the TTN kinase domain mutation revealed wild-type sequence in all subjects.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) described 11 patients from 5 British families with the TTN p.C30071R mutation. Onset was typically in the fourth or fifth decade with tripping, falling, myalgia and walking difficulty; CK ranged from normal to 1195 IU/L; the course was slowly progressive with proximal, distal and axial involvement, and only 1 patient lost ambulation after about 25 years. Ten of 11 had abnormal pulmonary function indicating respiratory muscle weakness, and 4 required nocturnal noninvasive ventilation 20 to 30 years after onset. Newly noted features included often asymmetric scapular winging, elbow and/or Achilles tendon contractures, variable spinal rigidity, and muscle hypertrophy; cardiac involvement was mild left ventricular impairment in 1 and supraventricular tachycardia in 1.
quotes: Onset was typically in the 4th or 5th decades, and symptoms included tripping and falling, myalgia and walking difficulties. CK values ranged from normal levels to 1195 IU/L (average 730 IU/L).

Ten of 11 patients had abnormal pulmonary function tests indicative of respiratory muscle weakness, and requirement for nocturnal noninvasive ventilation occurred approximately 20-30 years after disease onset in 4 patients.
Previously undocumented examination findings in this condition included scapular winging, often asymmetrical, elbow and/or achilles tendon (TA) contractures and a variable degree of spinal rigidity.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) reported muscle MRI in 3 patients with the p.C30071R mutation showing early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles, including a presymptomatic individual.
quotes: Findings were consistent with previous reports, with early involvement of the semitendinosus and peroneus longus muscles.
This presymptomatic individual with the p.C30071R mutation has the characteristic damage pattern of fatty infiltration in the peroneus longus and semitendinosus muscles.

phenotypes.text: fatty infiltration of semitendinosus and peroneus longus

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that muscle biopsies of p.C30071R patients showed myopathic or dystrophic changes; rimmed vacuoles in 3, eosinophilic and dark blue Gomori trichrome inclusions in 3, and cytoplasmic accumulation of desmin, myotilin, p62 and ubiquitin in 6 of 7 biopsies. Three biopsies showed cytoplasmic aggregates with a 'cheetah skin' appearance, particularly with myotilin staining, and inclusions did not fully overlap with protein accumulations. The authors concluded these features supported a diagnosis of MFM.
quotes: Rimmed vacuoles were observed in 3 biopsies, while eosinophilic inclusions and dark blue inclusions on G-Tri staining were present in 3 biopsies
Variable degrees of cytoplasmic accumulation of desmin, myotilin, P62 and ubiquitin was present in 6/7 biopsies.
In three biopsies (F.1B, F.4A and F.5), cytoplasmic aggregates showed a “cheetah skin appearance”, particularly with myotilin staining (Figure 4).

phenotypes.text: cytoplasmic accumulation of desmin and myotilin

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) found that probands of 5 new families and 3 previously reported families with p.C30071R shared a common core haplotype of 171 kb on chromosome 2; the probability of this sharing in 8 unrelated families by chance was less than 10(-6). The small shared region suggested an ancient mutation, and the authors attributed the frequency of the mutation (5.5% of undiagnosed UK MFM patients) to a British founder effect.
quotes: Analysis of polymorphic markers on chromosome 2 in probands from families F.1-5 and the previously reported 3 families with the p.C30071R mutation showed a common haplotype that included rs6706354, rs6706483, rs919177, and the p.C30071R mutation, indicating a core region of 171 kbp.
The very small size of the shared haplotype suggests an ancient mutation
The finding of the p.C30071R mutation in 3.9% of our study population is likely due to a British founder effect.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) identified a novel heterozygous TTN variant, g.274436C>T (p.P30091L), at a highly conserved residue in the 119th FN3 domain, in a patient (F.6) with adult-onset MFM-compatible myopathy with proximal weakness, mild neck weakness, calf hypertrophy, scapular winging, respiratory involvement (FVC 52%), and biopsy showing rimmed vacuoles and myotilin/p62 accumulation. The variant was absent from 400 control chromosomes but was also carried by a healthy 61-year-old brother, suggesting it may be neutral, although reduced penetrance could not be excluded.
quotes: Analysis of family F.6 revealed that the 61 year old brother of the proband is a healthy carrier of the g.274436C>T/p.P30091L variant.
The p.P30091L variant found in subject F.6 was also identified in an unaffected brother, suggesting that p.P30091L is a neutral variant.
Patient F.6 showed mild neck weakness and calf hypertrophy. Scapular winging was present in both patients, and patient F.6 had respiratory involvement.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) identified a novel heterozygous TTN variant, g.274599C>G (p.N30145K), in the 119th FN3 domain in a patient from Brazil (F.7) with adult-onset proximal limb weakness, severe ankle dorsiflexion weakness, scapular winging, and several affected relatives who were unavailable. MRI showed semitendinosus, tibialis anterior and peroneus longus involvement, and biopsy showed rimmed vacuoles and cytoplasmic bodies. The variant was absent from 400 control chromosomes; segregation could not be assessed.
quotes: Two additional subjects had novel heterozygous variants in the FN3 domain (g.274436C>T, p.P30091L in F.6 and g.274599C>G, p.N30145K in F.7).
Patient F.7, originally from Brazil, has several affected family members but none were available for clinical assessment.

In the absence of segregation analysis, we cannot further comment on the p.N30145K variant identified in subject F.7, although MRI findings were supportive of a diagnosis of MFM-titinopathy (Figure 3).

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) proposed that hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (HMERF) due to TTN mutations be classified nosologically as MFM-titinopathy.
quotes: We suggest that HMERF due to mutations in the TTN gene be nosologically classified as MFM-titinopathy.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2014) recommended sequencing the 119th FN3 domain of TTN in the diagnostic workup of MFM, particularly with early respiratory involvement and supportive muscle MRI, and recommended cardiac surveillance for patients with TTN mutations. They cautioned that TTN is highly polymorphic, with 71 novel coding variants found in exome data from 239 subjects, none in the 119th FN3 domain.
quotes: sequencing of this FN3 domain of TTN should be performed as part of the diagnostic workup for MFM, particularly in the presence of early respiratory involvement and supportive muscle MRI.
Exome data from 239 subjects at our centre discovered 71 novel TTN coding changes of uncertain significance.
we recommend cardiac surveillance for all patients with TTN mutations

relevance_reason: Identifies the TTN p.Cys30071Arg mutation segregating with hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure in three families and defines the phenotype.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) used genome-wide linkage combined with whole exome sequencing in a family with autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and identified a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2 containing the likely causal variant in TTN.
quotes: A combination of genome-wide linkage and whole exome sequencing revealed the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg) within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) identified a variant in the TTN gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg) that segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, 9 subjects in a second family with the same selective pattern of muscle involvement on MRI, and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.
quotes: A combination of genome-wide linkage and whole exome sequencing revealed the likely causal genetic variant in the titin (TTN) gene (g.274375T>C; p.Cys30071Arg) within a shared haplotype of 2.93 Mbp on chromosome 2.

This segregated with the phenotype in 21 individuals from the original family, nine subjects in a second family with the same highly selective pattern of muscle involvement on magnetic resonance imaging and a third familial case with a similar phenotype.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) defined the phenotype in 31 TTN mutation carriers followed for up to 31 years. Presentation included predominant distal, proximal, or respiratory muscle weakness, with highly variable age of onset from early adulthood to a mild phenotype in advanced age; weakness was earlier and more severe in the lower extremities in nearly all patients, 7 had axial weakness, respiratory function deteriorated gradually over time, and no patient had cardiomyopathy.
quotes: The clinical presentation included predominant distal, proximal or respiratory muscle weakness. The age of onset was highly variable, from early adulthood, and including a mild phenotype in advanced age.
Muscle weakness was earlier onset and more severe in the lower extremities in nearly all patients. Seven patients also had axial muscle weakness.
Cardiomyopathy was not present in any of our patients despite up to 31 years of follow-up.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) performed muscle MRI in 21 affected patients and found characteristic abnormalities with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21, including 3 presymptomatic patients. Muscle histopathology most frequently showed eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles but was nonspecific in a minority.
quotes: Magnetic resonance muscle imaging was performed in 21 affected patients and revealed characteristic abnormalities with semitendinosus involvement in 20 of 21 patients studied, including 3 patients who were presymptomatic.
Diagnostic muscle histopathology most frequently revealed eosinophilic inclusions (inclusion bodies) and rimmed vacuoles, but was non-specific in a minority of patients.

findings.statement: Pfeffer et al. (2012) suggested that the disease be considered in patients with adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy and early respiratory failure, even with nonspecific pathology, that muscle MRI be an initial investigation prompting TTN screening if positive, and that whole exome sequencing provides a reliable cost-effective approach to screening the 363-exon TTN gene.
quotes: This disease should be considered in patients with adult-onset proximal or distal myopathy and early respiratory failure, even in the presence of non-specific muscle pathology.
Muscle magnetic resonance imaging findings are characteristic and should be considered as an initial investigation, and if positive should prompt screening for mutations in TTN.

relevance_reason: Muscle MRI characterization of patients with autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure (Edstrom myopathy/MFM9), defining selective muscle involvement useful for diagnosis.

findings.statement: Birchall et al. (2005) performed muscle MRI on 7 patients (age range 37-66 years, 4 male) with autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure, a dominant limb myopathy with insidious onset in late adult life in which respiratory failure occurs while patients are still ambulant. MRI showed selective early involvement of the semitendinosus and obturator externus muscles that could not be detected clinically, with different rates of progression in closely related muscles.
quotes: We recently described a dominant limb myopathy characterised by early respiratory failure whilst affected individuals were still ambulant (autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure).

We performed muscle magnetic resonance imaging on seven cases of autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure (age range 37-66 years, 4 male) and show selective early involvement of semitendinosus and obturator externus on magnetic resonance imaging that cannot be detected clinically

phenotypes.text: selective semitendinosus and obturator externus involvement on muscle MRI

findings.statement: Birchall et al. (2005) concluded that subclinical semitendinosus and obturator externus involvement on muscle MRI is specific to autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and enables early noninvasive diagnosis of at-risk individuals, which is otherwise difficult because of the insidious late-adult onset and highly selective clinical and pathologic muscle involvement.
quotes: Early diagnosis and exclusion of this disorder is difficult because of the insidious onset in late adult life and the highly selective muscle involvement, both clinically and pathologically.
These findings are specific to autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and enable early non-invasive diagnosis for individuals at risk.

relevance_reason: The abstract reports that a human mutation in the titin kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting a TK–nbr1–p62–MuRF2 signaling pathway. This is the mechanism and molecular basis of hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure. Only the abstract was available, so the variant, the patients and the clinical details are not given.

findings.statement: Lange et al. (2005) identified a signaling complex in which the titin protein kinase domain (TK) interacts with the zinc-finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation. Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated protein p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres. p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific RING-B-box E3 ligase that binds the transactivation domain of serum response factor (SRF).
quotes: We identified a signaling complex where TK interacts with the zinc-finger protein nbr1 through a mechanically inducible conformation.

Nbr1 targets the ubiquitin-associated p62/SQSTM1 to sarcomeres, and p62 in turn interacts with MuRF2, a muscle-specific RING-B-box E3 ligase and ligand of the transactivation domain of the serum response transcription factor (SRF).

findings.statement: Lange et al. (2005) found that mechanical inactivity induced MuRF2 to move into the nucleus. This reduced nuclear SRF and repressed transcription, which suggests that the titin kinase domain controls muscle gene expression and protein turnover in response to mechanical load.
quotes: Nuclear translocation of MuRF2 was induced by mechanical inactivity and caused reduction of nuclear SRF and repression of transcription.

findings.statement: Lange et al. (2005) reported that a human mutation in the titin (TTN) protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting the TK–nbr1–p62–MuRF2 signaling pathway.
quotes: A human mutation in the titin protein kinase domain causes hereditary muscle disease by disrupting this pathway.

relevance_reason: This paper describes the original family with an autosomal dominant distal myopathy and early respiratory failure, which matches the subject of this MFM9 entry. It covers the clinical features and pathology and excludes linkage to the known distal myopathy loci.

findings.statement: Chinnery et al. (2001) described a novel autosomal dominant myopathy in a 3-generation family. Affected members presented in mid-adult life with weakness of the tibialis anterior. The authors clinically assessed 24 individuals, 11 of whom were affected. Affected members of the second generation presented at an earlier age, and their disease progressed more rapidly than in the first generation. Weakness of the hip girdle and shoulder girdle appeared later in the course.
quotes: We describe a novel autosomal dominant myopathy presenting in mid-adult life with tibialis anterior weakness.
We carried out a detailed clinical assessment of 24 individuals spanning three generations, documenting pathologic features of the muscles in 7 of the 11 affected individuals
The second generation of affected individuals presented at an earlier age, and the disease progressed more rapidly than in the first generation.

findings.statement: In this family, Chinnery et al. (2001) found on lung function testing a progressive global weakness of the respiratory muscles that could be detected from the time of presentation. In some cases the diaphragm was preferentially involved.
quotes: Lung function tests revealed progressive global respiratory muscle weakness detectable from the time of presentation, with preferential diaphragmatic involvement in some cases.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

findings.statement: Chinnery et al. (2001) studied muscle pathology in 7 of the 11 affected individuals, including 1 at autopsy, and found that pathology correlated closely with clinical involvement. Muscles that were clinically unaffected showed minimal change. Moderately affected muscles showed fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and rimmed vacuoles with basophilic rims. In severely involved muscles, the muscle fibers had been replaced by fat and fibrous connective tissue. The inclusions were Congophilic and reacted with antibodies to desmin, beta-amyloid, and phosphorylated tau protein.
quotes: Fiber splitting, eosinophilic inclusions, and vacuoles with basophilic rims were seen in moderately affected muscles, and fat and fibrous connective tissue replaced muscle fibers in the severely involved muscles.
The inclusions were Congophilic and reacted with antibodies to desmin, beta-amyloid, and phosphorylated tau protein.
Clinically unaffected muscles had minimal pathologic change.

phenotypes.text: eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions with desmin, beta-amyloid, and phosphorylated tau immunoreactivity
fatty and fibrous replacement of muscle

findings.statement: Chinnery et al. (2001) found that the disease in this family was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies. They concluded that the disorder is genetically and phenotypically distinct.
quotes: The disease was not linked to any of the known loci associated with distal myopathies, confirming that the disorder in this family is both genetically and phenotypically distinct.

relevance_reason: Reports a French family with a phenotype like the Swedish 2q24-q31 myopathy that was excluded from that region and mapped to 2q21, which is evidence of genetic heterogeneity.

findings.statement: Xiang et al. (1999) studied a French family with autosomal dominant myopathy. The family's clinical phenotype and muscle biopsy findings were similar to those of the Swedish families with proximal muscle weakness and early respiratory muscle involvement mapped to 2q24-q31. However, the 2q24-q31 region was completely excluded in the French family.
quotes: a French family with a similar clinical phenotype and pathology (muscle biopsy) was investigated to see whether the disease gene associated with the myopathy is mapped to the same region as the one in the Swedish families; however, chromosomal region 2q24-q31 was completely excluded.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

findings.statement: Xiang et al. (1999) performed a genome-wide scan with polymorphic microsatellite markers in the French family. They obtained a maximum two-point lod score of 2.11, the highest achievable in this family, for markers in a 4-cM region between D2S1272 and D2S1260. The authors suggested that the gene for the French form is likely located on chromosome 2q21.
quotes: A maximum two-point lod score of 2.11 (the highest lod score that can be achieved in this family) was obtained for the markers in the region between D2S1272 and D2S1260, spanning 4 cM.
This result suggests that the gene responsible for the French form is likely to be located on chromosome 2q21.

relevance_reason: Reports the clinical phenotype and the linkage mapping of the disorder (autosomal dominant myopathy with early respiratory failure and cytoplasmic bodies) to 2q24-q31 in two Swedish families.

findings.statement: Nicolao et al. (1999) studied 2 Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy. Affected members had proximal weakness and early respiratory failure, and their muscle biopsies showed characteristic cytoplasmic bodies.
quotes: Two Swedish families with autosomal dominant myopathy, who also had proximal weakness, early respiratory failure, and characteristic cytoplasmic bodies in the affected muscle biopsies

findings.statement: Nicolao et al. (1999) ran a genome-wide linkage screen in 2 Swedish families and mapped the disease to chromosome 2q24-q31. They obtained a maximum combined two-point LOD score of 4.87 at theta = 0 with marker D2S1245. Haplotype analysis placed the gene in a 17-cM region between D2S2384 and D2S364.
quotes: Linkage to the chromosomal region 2q24-q31 was established. A maximum combined two-point LOD score of 4.87 at a recombination fraction of 0 was obtained with marker D2S1245.
Haplotype analysis indicated that the gene responsible for the disease is likely to be located in the 17-cM region between markers D2S2384 and D2S364.

findings.statement: Nicolao et al. (1999) found that affected individuals from the 2 Swedish families shared an identical haplotype, which suggested a common origin.
quotes: The affected individuals from these two families share an identical haplotype, which suggests a common origin.

relevance_reason: Original clinical and pathological description of hereditary myopathy with early respiratory failure (Edstrom myopathy) in 16 patients from 7 pedigrees.

findings.statement: Edström et al. (1990) described 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with an unusual adult-onset limb-girdle myopathy. All patients had prominent early respiratory muscle weakness, and in many an acute respiratory incapacity prompted the first neurologic examination. Neck flexor weakness and sometimes foot extensor weakness were other early symptoms. Electrophysiologic analysis confirmed a myopathy, and serum muscle enzyme levels were normal or slightly elevated.
quotes: 16 patients representing 7 different pedigrees exhibited an unusual, adult onset limb-girdle myopathy with typical clinical hallmarks.
A prominent early finding in all cases was respiratory muscle weakness, and in many of these an acute respiratory incapacity was the reason for the first neurological examination.
Neck flexor and sometimes foot extensor weakness were other early symptoms.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness

phenotypes.text: normal or slightly elevated serum muscle enzymes

findings.statement: Edström et al. (1990) found evidence of autosomal dominant inheritance in the majority of the 16 patients from 7 pedigrees with myopathy and early respiratory failure.
quotes: In a majority of cases there was evidence of an autosomal dominant inheritance.

findings.statement: Edström et al. (1990) found myofibrillar changes on muscle biopsy, including plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, a marker for F-actin. Ultrastructurally, the plaques were composed of moderately dense thin filaments and were related to splitting of Z-discs or formed extensions from Z-discs.
quotes: Muscle biopsy findings revealed myofibrillar changes which, at the light microscopy level, included plaques that stained strongly with rhodamine-conjugated phalloidin, a specific marker for F-actin.
At the ultrastructural level, these plaques were observed to be composed of moderately dense, thin filaments and were related to splitting of Z-discs or formed extensions from Z-discs.

findings.statement: Edström et al. (1990) suggested that the muscle biopsy changes indicated defective myofibrillogenesis and discussed the possibility of defective actin polymerization.
quotes: We believe that the muscle biopsy changes revealed by cytochemical and ultrastructural observations indicate defective myofibrillogenesis, and the possibility of defective actin polymerization is discussed.
